field.name: SRWD
field.description: SRWD: SERDES Read/Write Data. Note: If this control port is not connected to the SERDES then these bits will always read as 8'h0

field.name: SRI
field.description: SRI: Read/Write indicator to SERDES bus controller. 1= Write, 0 = Read

enumeratedValue.name: Port00Addr
enumeratedValue.description: Address port 0 configuration / status register set

enumeratedValue.name: Port01Addr
enumeratedValue.description: Address port 1 configuration / status register set

field.name: TTA
field.description: TTA: This value determines the time period the Controller transmits and waits for ALIGNp during speed negotiation. This value is derived for the PM_CLK period

field.name: SNM
field.description: SNM: Speed Negotiation Method, when set to 1 the speed negotiation is run starting at gen1 speed up to fastest supported speed, when cleared to o the speed negotiation is run starting at the fastest supported speed down to gen1 speed

field.name: SNR
field.description: SNR: Speed Negotiation Rate, when set to 1 the speed negotiation is run only at the rate programmed in the SPD field of the SControl

field.name: FPR
field.description: FPR: Force PHY Ready. This signal determines how PhyReady is driven

enumeratedValue.name: frcPhyRdy
enumeratedValue.description: frcPhyRdy: In this mode the OOB and speed negotiation states of the Phy Init State machine are bypassed. The Phy Init state machine directly enters PhyReady after reset. Tx buffer IDLE control is forced off

field.name: PBPE
field.description: PBPE: PhyControl BIST Pattern Enable. Setting this bit to 1 enables the Phy Control Test Pattern generation

field.name: PBCE
field.description: PBCE: PhyControl BIST Clear Error. Setting this bit to 1 clears the pattern match error bit. When a pattern mismatch occurs this bit needs to be set then negated to clear the error

field.name: PBPNA
field.description: PBPNA: PhyControl BIST Pattern no Aligns. Setting this bit will cause the Phy Ctrl Pattern generator to transmit each pattern continuously

field.name: STB
field.description: STB: Status Bit. Reading this bit will show that status of the Gen Fixed clocks parameter. This bit indicates if the Phy Control layer is running from a fixed frequency clock or a variable clock derived from the tx clock of the SERDES

field.name: PSSO
field.description: PSSO: PhyControl select SERDES OOB or internally decoded OOB signaling as inputs

field.name: PSS
field.description: PSS: PhyControl select SERDES Slumber CMU during Link Slumber. When the controller enters slumber if this bit is set an extra control signal is applied to the Serdes to slumber the Clock block within the Serdes. This will yield extra power savings but is Serdes specific

field.name: ERSN
field.description: Enable reset speed negotiation (ERSN): If enabled then the Phy control layer will enable only a single speed on the Rx path during speed negotiation. This speed is determined as the fastest support for the first round falling to the lowest speed for the final round. Each round of speed negotiation is terminated by the host issuing a COMRESET and rerunning OOB before beginning the next round of speed negotiation as detailed in RSN Reset Speed Negotiation

field.name: ESDF
field.description: ESDF: Enable signal det filter, if set the a single de-assertion of signal detect or the coreRxDataValid when the Phy Init state machine is in the PhyReady state will cause the state machine to exit the PhyReady state and return to a PhyNotReady state, this will result in the OOB and speed negotiation running again

field.name: SFD
field.description: SFD: Signal Failure Detection, if the signal detection de-asserts for a time greater than this then the OOB detector will determine this is a line idle and cause the PhyInit state machine to exit the Phy Ready State. A value of zero disables the Signal Failure Detector. The value is based on the OOB Detector Clock typically (PMCLK Clock Period) * SFD giving a nominal time of 500ns based on a 150MHz PMCLK

field.name: PTST
field.description: PTST: Partial to Slumber timer value, specific delay the controller should apply while in partial before entering slumber. The value is bases on the system clock divided by 128, total delay = (Sys Clock Period) * PTST * 128

field.name: RIT
field.description: RIT: Retry Interval Timer. The calculated value divided by two, the lower digit of precision is not needed

field.name: RCT
field.description: RCT: Rate Change Timer, a value based on the 54.2us for which a SATA device will transmit at a fixed rate ALIGNp after OOB has completed, for a fast SERDES it is suggested that this value be 54.2us / 4

field.name: ARCA
field.description: Address Read Cache ATAPI (ARCA): This is the value driven onto ARCACHE when the AXI master is posting a data burst or ATAPI FIS read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARCF
field.description: Address Read Cache FIS (ARCF): This is the value driven onto ARCACHE when the AXI master is posting a command FIS read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARCH
field.description: Address Read Cache Header (ARCH): This is the value driven onto ARCACHE when the AXI master is posting a Header or physical region descriptor read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARCP
field.description: Address Read Cache PRD (ARCP): This is the value driven onto ARCACHE when the AXI master is posting a PRD read address to the memory controller

field.name: AWCFD
field.description: Address Write Cache Final Data (AWCFD): This is the value driven onto AWCACHE when the AXI master is posting a Data burst write address to the memory controller when the data burst is the final burst in the transfer

field.name: AWCD
field.description: Address Write Cache Data (AWCD): This is the value driven onto AWCACHE when the AXI master is posting a Data burst write address to the memory controller when the data burst is not the final burst in the transfer

field.name: AWCF
field.description: Address Write Cache FIS (AWCF): This is the value driven onto AWCACHE when the AXI master is posting a status FIS write address to the memory controller

field.name: EARC
field.description: Enable the ARCACHE (EARC): control from the PRDT entries used during the data phase of this operation (Global Control)

field.name: MAWID
field.description: Memory Address write ID (MAWID): for non data transfers

field.name: MAWIDD
field.description: Memory Address write ID (MAWIDD): for data transfers

field.name: MARID
field.description: Memory Address read ID (MARID): for non data transfers

field.name: MARIDD
field.description: Memory Address Read ID (MARIDD): for data transfers

field.name: OTL
field.description: Outstanding Transfer Limit (OTL): This limits the maximum number of outstanding transfers supported: a) for the 264 DWords Transport Layer implementation this can be programmed between 1 and 16 b) for the 136 DWord Transport Layer implementation this can be programmed between 1 and 8 c) for the 72 DWord Transport Layer implementation this can be programmed between 1 and 4 0 = Transfers limited by the transport Layer FIFO space / fill level

field.name: ECM
field.description: Enable the Context management (ECM): system in the memory

field.name: AAO
field.description: Allow Address Overwrite (AAO): Command List Base Address [9:0] and FIS Base Address [7:0] to be overwritten

field.name: AXIPE
field.description: AXI Parity Enable (AXIPE): Parity Checking is enabled in the Link layer. The Parity is generated and checked on each byte within the 128 bit data busses on the Master interface

field.name: AXIPT
field.description: AXI Parity Type (AXIPT): 1 = Odd Parity, 0 = Even Parity

field.name: EDAS
field.description: Enable Data Auto Start (EDAS): When set if the controller receives a PIO or DMA Setup for read Data it will begin fetching PRD entries to accelerate the data reception phase

field.name: ARPD
field.description: Address Read Prot Data (ARPD): This is the value driven onto ARPROT when the AXI master is posting a data burst read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARPF
field.description: Address Read Prot FIS (ARPF): This is the value driven onto ARPROT when the AXI master is posting a command FIS read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARPH
field.description: Address Read Prot Header (ARPH): This is the value driven onto ARPROT when the AXI master is posting a Header read address to the memory controller

field.name: ARPP
field.description: Address Read Prot PRD (ARPP): This is the value driven onto ARPROT when the AXI master is posting a PRD read address to the memory controller

field.name: AWPFD
field.description: Address Write Prot Final Data (AWPFD): This is the value driven onto AWPROT when the AXI master is posting a Data burst write address to the memory controller when the data burst is the final burst in the transfer

field.name: AWPD
field.description: Address Write Prot Data (AWPD): This is the value driven onto AWPROT when the AXI master is posting a Data burst write address to the memory controller when the data burst is not the final burst in the transfer

field.name: AWPF
field.description: Address Write Prot FIS (AWPF): This is the value driven onto AWPROT when the AXI master is posting a status FIS write address to the memory controller

field.name: EAWP
field.description: Enable the AWPROT (EAWP): control from the PRDT entries used during the data phase of this operation

field.name: EARP
field.description: Enable the ARPROT (EARP): control from the PRDT entries used during the data phase of this operation

field.name: RXWM
field.description: RxWaterMark (RXWM): This sets the minimum number of free location within the RX FIFO before the watermark is exceeded which in turn will cause the Transport Layer to instruct the Link Layer to transmit HOLDS to the transmitting end. Note that it can take some time for the HOLDs to get to the other end and that in the interim there must be enough room in the FIFO to absorb all data that could arrive. An initial value of 7'h20 is recommended

field.name: ENBD
field.description: Enable Back down (ENBD): When a port multiplier is attached if an attempt to send a command to an attached drive results in 3 consecutive retries due to an R_ERR receptions then the command removed for the transport layer and returned to the pending queue. This is to avoid unnecessary retries owing to the device trying to send a Set device bits FIS while the host is trying to send a command. This feature should improve performance as it allows the controller queue any pending commands to the other drives

field.name: ITM
field.description: Initialise Transport Memories (ITM): When set this will cause the memory initialise hardware state machine to enter reset, when cleared the machine will run writing zero to all locations within the memory

field.name: TXBC
field.description: Tx Bad CRC (TXBC): A bad CRC (inverted value of the correct CRC) value will be transmitted for one FIS only by the Link Layer when a rising edge is detected on this signal. This bit has to be toggled from a '0' to a '1' to enable this feature

field.name: RXBC
field.description: Rx Bad CRC (RXBC): When a rising edge is detected on this bit, it causes a bad CRC to be detected for the current frame. This bit has to be toggled from a '0' to a '1' to enable this feature

field.name: TXC
field.description: Tx Cont (TXC): If this bit is asserted, then the transmission of CONT primitives is enabled. If de-asserted, then long sequences of repeated primitives can be sent by the Link Layer

field.name: TXPJ
field.description: Tx Prim Junk (TXPJ): If this bit is de-asserted, then scrambled junk data is sent after a CONT primitive, as per the Serial ATA specification. If this bit is asserted, then the single character 32'hDEADBEEF is sent continuously instead. This is to aid debug

field.name: TXSE
field.description: Tx Scramble Enable (TXSE): If this bit is asserted then scrambling of the Transmit data is enabled as per the Serial ATA specification

field.name: RXSE
field.description: Rx Scramble Enable (RXSE): If this bit is asserted then de-scrambling of the Receive data is enabled as per the Serial ATA specification

field.name: S4A
field.description: Send 4 Aligns (S4A): When asserted, four ALIGN primitives are transmitted at the specified rate, instead of the normal two ALIGNS

field.name: EPNRT
field.description: Enable Phy Not Ready Timer (EPNRT): If PhyReady is de-asserted for a length of time, as specified by Phy Ready Timer, then this bit, when asserted, enables the Link Layer to re-issue a PhyReset, thereby re-initiating OOB

field.name: AIR
field.description: Align Insertion Rate (AIR): The Serial ATA specification requires that the Link Layer sends a pair of ALIGN primitives at least every 254 DWords of data. This is achieved by setting Align Insertion Rate to "11111111". However, for test purposes it is possible to send ALIGNs at a higher rate. This can be achieved by setting Align Insertion Rate to a lower value i.e. (Align Insertion Rate-1) DWords will be sent by the Link Layer between each set of ALIGN primitive pairs. Note: If Send 4 Aligns is set, one should not set the Align Insertion Rate to be four or less. If Send 4 Aligns is not set, one should not set the Align Insertion Rate to be two or less

field.name: PRT
field.description: Phy Ready Timer (PRT): These 10 bits specify the timeout value of the PhyReady Timer. If EnPhyReadyTimeOut is set, the Link Layer will count down on every rising edge of txWordClk, as long as PhyReady is de-asserted. When the counter reaches zero, a PhyReset will be issued to the Phy to try and re-establish communications with the far-end. The timer is initially loaded with a value equal to the concatenation of { Phy Ready Timer, 9'h000}

field.name: POE
field.description: Primitive Override Enable (POE): When set, this bit enables the replacement of a single primitive, as specified by Override Primitive/CD, when the Link Layer state machine is in the Prim Override State. This bit has to be toggled from a '0' to a '1' to enable this feature

field.name: PMPRA
field.description: Power Management Primitive Rate Acknowledge (PMPRA): This value determines the number of PMACK primitives sent when a power management state transition is requested by the host

field.name: POS
field.description: Primitive Override State (POS): These 6 bits are used in the Primitive Override Debug functionality. When the Link Layer detects a positive edge on Primitive Override Enable, it overrides the next primitive that would be inserted during the Prim Override State, with the data specified by the Override Primitive and CD configuration bits

field.name: CD
field.description: Data Character or Primitive (CD): This bit specifies whether the data used during the primitive override should be a data character or a primitive. E.g. if CD = 1, Prim Override State = L_SendEOF and Override Primitive = WTRM, then a WTRM primitive will be inserted into the data stream instead of an EOF (whenever a rising edge is seen on Primitive Override Enable). If CD = 0, then a normal data character (as specified by Override Primitive) is inserted into the data stream instead of the EOF

field.name: OP
field.description: Override Primitive (OP): This 32-bit bus specifies the data to be used in the overriding primitive debug logic, described in the definition of LinkCfg1 above

field.name: LLS
field.description: LAT_LINK_STATE (LLS): These six bits specify the current value of the Link Layer State Machine at the time the Status0 register is read

field.name: DMBW
field.description: DMA Master bus width (DMBW): 0 = 32 bit, 1 = 64 bit, 2 = 128 bit

field.name: DMB
field.description: DMA Master bus type (DMB): 0 = AHB, 1 = AXI

field.name: SVN
field.description: SATA Version (SVN): indicates the version of the SATA protocol supported by the controller. 1 = GEN1, 2 = GEN2, 3 = GEN3

field.name: DEC
field.description: Disparity Error Count (DEC): The number of DWords that have been received from the Phy, where one or more disparity errors have been detected. A value of 255 indicates an error count of 255 or more as this counter does not wrap around to zero. The count value is updated with its current value each time the Status1 register is read

field.name: CEC
field.description: Code Error Count (CEC): The number of DWords that have been received from the Phy, where one or more code errors have been detected. A value of 255 indicates an error count of 255 or more as this counter does not wrap around to zero. The count value is updated with its current value each time the Status1 register is read

field.name: PIEC
field.description: Phy Internal Error Count (PIEC): The number of DWords that have been received from the Phy, where one or more internal errors have been detected. A value of 255 indicates an error count of 255 or more as this counter does not wrap around to zero. The count value is updated with its current value each time the Status1 register is read

field.name: KCEC
field.description: Kchar Error Count (KCEC): The number of DWords that have been received from the Phy, where one or more control character errors have been detected. A value of 255 indicates an error count of 255 or more as this counter does not wrap around to zero. The count value is updated with its current value each time the Status1 register is read

field.name: ETLLB
field.description: Enable Transport Layer Loopback in the BIST L Mode (ETLLB)

field.name: TSVT
field.description: Trustzone Slave ID of violating transaction (TSVT): When the Slave Port rejects a read or write as Slave Error due to security violation, this register records the AXI ID of the violating transaction

field.name: TSVIE
field.description: Trustzone Slave ID violation interrupt Enable (TSVIE): The interrupt will be seen on Interrupt status bit 3 in the general register group

field.name: PHYD
field.description: Current 16 bit Data (PHYD): snapshot within the Phy Control Layer

field.name: PHYKC
field.description: Current 1 bit K Character (PHYKC): snapshot within the Phy Control Layer

field.name: PHYDE
field.description: Current 2 bit Disparity Error (PHYDE): snapshot within the Phy Control Layer

field.name: PHYCE
field.description: Current 2 bit Code Error (PHYCE): snapshot within the Phy Control Layer

field.name: TPS
field.description: Timer PreScalar value. (TPS) The system clock is divided by the ratio to generate a 10us clock pulse to run the port layers

enumeratedValue.name: VER_2
enumeratedValue.description: Second version, added support for SHA-256 algorithm (This is the value on this device).

field.name: PCCR2
field.description: Forces all cacheable spaces to write through

field.name: PCCR3
field.description: Forces no allocation on cache misses (must also have PCCR2 asserted)

enumeratedValue.name: INVW0_1
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, invalidate all lines in way 0.

enumeratedValue.name: PUSHW0_1
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, push all modified lines in way 0

enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, invalidate all lines in way 1

enumeratedValue.name: PUSHW1_1

enumeratedValue.name: LGO_0

enumeratedValue.name: LGO_1
enumeratedValue.description: Write: initiate line command indicated by bits CLCR[27:24]. Read: line command active.

enumeratedValue.name: INVW0_1
enumeratedValue.description: When setting the GO bit, invalidate all lines in way 0.

enumeratedValue.name: PUSHW0_1

enumeratedValue.name: INVW1_1
